claims.text: The as-deposited FeMnNiGeSi alloy is an ordered, single-phase hexagonal high-entropy alloy.
The as-deposited alloy undergoes a sharp first-order magnetostructural transition.
The as-deposited alloy has a large, hysteretic magnetocaloric response.
The as-deposited alloy contains few nano-twin boundaries or other interfacial nucleation features.
The scarcity of nano-twin boundaries and refined interfaces largely governs the sharpness and hysteresis of the magnetostructural transition.
Controlled low-level cold drawing can introduce nano-scale twin boundaries into the alloy.
A moderate deformation level can induce nano-twins without producing unwanted secondary phases or compromising mechanical stability.
Cold drawing increases the density of nano-twin boundaries and interfacial features.
Deformation-induced nano-twin boundaries provide additional, more uniformly distributed nucleation sites for the magnetostructural transition.
The additional nucleation sites lower local energy barriers during the magnetostructural transition.
Lower and more uniformly distributed nucleation barriers produce a more homogeneous and gradual transition pathway.
The deformed sample will exhibit a broader magnetocaloric peak than the as-deposited control.
The deformed sample will exhibit less hysteresis than the as-deposited control.
The peak entropy change of the deformed sample may be modestly lower than that of the as-deposited control.
The predictions apply to low-field magnetic-cooling cycles near the nominal magnetostructural transition temperature.
A hysteresis reduction of less than approximately 10% relative to the control is designated as a falsifying outcome.
Failure to observe a measurable increase in nano-twin density after cold drawing is designated as a falsifying outcome.
